draft.title: Changing form and medium
card: Form is the kind of text, such as a play, novel, poem or film. Medium is the channel that carries it, such as a stage, a page or a screen.
Each form has its own tools. A film can use close-ups, music and editing. A play relies on live actors, dialogue, staging and lighting. A novel can take the reader inside a character's thoughts.
When a story moves to a new form, the composer must change how it is told. Some things are shown in a new way, some are cut and some are added.
Because the form changes the telling, it also changes the meaning a reader or viewer takes away. Comparing the two forms is part of the conversation between the texts.
draft.remember: A new form gives a story new tools, so the same story can mean something different.

a.q: Why does moving a story from a novel to a film change how it is told?
opts: Each form has different tools for showing events and ideas
Films must always follow the plot of the novel exactly
A film can only tell a story through spoken dialogue
The meaning of a story stays the same in any form
a.why: A novel can describe thoughts in words, while a film must use images, sound and editing. The tools differ, so the telling differs. It is wrong to say the meaning stays the same, because the new tools change what the audience notices.
a.clue: Think about the tools each form has available.

b.q: A novel tells us a girl's fear through several pages of her private thoughts. In the film version, the director shows a close-up of her shaking hands and uses a low, tense soundtrack. What does this change show?
opts: The film uses its own tools to convey the same feeling
The film has left out the girl's fear completely
The film is a weaker text because it uses no words
The film has changed the story's setting and period
b.why: The close-up and soundtrack are film techniques that replace the novel's access to thoughts. The fear is still there, but it is shown in a new way. It is not a weaker text, because each form has its own strengths.
b.clue: Ask what the film does in place of describing thoughts.

a.best: Each form has different tools for showing events and ideas

b.best: The film uses its own tools to convey the same feeling

problems.detail: Why (a) says a film 'must use images, sound and editing', but the card says a film 'can use' these tools. Films can also convey thoughts in words, through voiceover, dialogue or on-screen text, so 'must' overstates the point.
The clue 'Think about the tools each form has available' repeats the key word 'tools' from the right option, which gives the answer away.
